newsitem.title: UK: Schroders, MAM leap on bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Schroders, MAM leap on bid talk.

text.p: Shares in British investment bank Schroders Plc and fund management group Mercury Asset Management Plc shot higher on Friday amid a renewed bout of bid talk, dealers said.
Dealers said the latest burst of stock market strength, with the FTSE 100 index reaching a record 4,287.2, was another positive factor as it lifted the value of their investment holdings.
But they said it was the talk of a takeover bid in the sector that propelled the stocks higher. "People are all talking about a bid for MAMs or Schroders," one market-maker said.
Some said there was vague talk of a bid from U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch and Co Inc after this week's surprise merger between Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover & Co.
Schroders was up 60p at 17.50 stg by 1000 GMT while MAM was up 44-1/2 at 13.57-1/2 stg.
Trading volume in both stocks was relatively thin at 49,773 and 479,701 shares respectively.
Elsewhere in the fund management sector, M&G Group Plc was up 27-1/2p at 13.80 stg and Perpetual Plc was up 25p at 26.40 stg.
Bid speculation around the likes of Schroders and MAM is nothing new, dating back at least to the takeover of S.G. Warburg by Swiss Bank in July 1995.
Warburg had held a major stake in MAM and had been in talks on a merger with Morgan Stanley. These were said to have been scuppered in part by MAM's opposition to the plan.
